revision_rule.note: The 2012 grammar differs materially: property case-item semicolons are optional and sequence actual arguments do not include the unbounded $ form.
The 2017 sequence_actual_arg production does not include the standalone $ alternative that is present in the 2023 grammar.
The 2012 block-item grammar additionally permits an optionally attributed overload_declaration.
The 2012 inside-case grammar uses open ranges and does not provide the later tolerance range forms using +/- or +%-.
The 2017 case-inside range grammar lacks the 2023 [expression +/- expression] and [expression +%- expression] tolerance-range forms.
The 2012 checker declaration alternatives additionally include overload_declaration, and its generate-item production uses elaboration_system_task.
The 2012 grammar has no interface-class item productions and uses tf_port_list rather than the later constructor-argument forms.
The 2017 grammar lacks interface-class items and the 2023 constructor argument-list alternatives that permit default arguments.
The 2012 `{ }` production is empty_queue rather than the later empty_unpacked_array_concatenation production.
The 2012 grammar lacks dynamic override specifiers, parenthesized array-method primaries, default distribution items, and their later declaration forms.
The 2017 grammar lacks dynamic override specifiers, parenthesized array built-in constraint primaries, and the default distribution item added to the 2023 productions.
The 2012 constraint-primary production has no parenthesized array built-in method form or corresponding parentheses guarantee.
The 2017 constraint_primary production has no parenthesized form; 2023 permits parentheses specifically for array built-in methods.
The 2012 class-constructor grammar has no default constructor-argument marker.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no default marker in a class constructor argument list, so no corresponding at-most-once rule exists.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no covergroup extends declaration form.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no covergroup extends declaration form.
The 2012 grammar lacks inherited covergroups, open-ended and tolerance covergroup ranges, and the $ integer coverage expression alternative.
The 2017 covergroup grammar lacks inherited covergroups and the open-ended and tolerance covergroup range productions present in 2023.
The 2012 param_assignment uses unpacked dimensions, and type_assignment permits only data_type rather than the later variable-dimension and incomplete class-scoped type forms.
In 2017 param_assignment uses unpacked dimensions rather than the broader 2023 variable dimensions, and type_assignment lacks the 2023 incomplete class-scoped type alternative.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no dynamic override specifier construct.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define dynamic override specifiers.
IEEE 1800-2012 instead requires `{}` to be legal only in the context of a queue.
The 2012 inside expression uses open_range_list without later tolerance ranges, and a tagged-union payload is an expression rather than the later primary form.
The 2017 tagged-union payload admits an expression rather than the 2023 primary, and its inside-expression range grammar lacks the 2023 tolerance ranges.
The 2012 function declaration and prototype productions do not admit dynamic override specifiers.
The 2017 function declaration and prototype productions do not admit the dynamic override specifiers added in 2023.
The 2012 rule permits a genvar identifier as a constant primary only within a genvar_expression, rather than anywhere within a loop generate construct.
IEEE 1800-2017 restricts a genvar constant primary to a genvar_expression, whereas 2023 states the broader loop-generate-construct context.
The 2012 identifier families differ, including interface_instance_identifier and production_identifier, and its ps_type_identifier lacks the later class_scope alternative.
The 2017 identifier productions lack the interface_port_identifier and rs_production_identifier families present in 2023.
The 2012 grammar places attributed modport declarations under interface_or_generate_item rather than directly among non-port interface items.
The 2012 elaboration_system_task production is the same accepted severity-task syntax under the earlier nonterminal name.
The 2012 type grammar lacks interface-class types, soft unions, and incomplete class-scoped type-reference forms.
The 2017 grammar lacks interface-class types, soft tagged unions, and incomplete class-scoped type-reference alternatives added by 2023.
The 2012 grammar requires a non-zero unsigned number for a literal size, whereas the 2023 production uses unsigned_number.
The 2017 size production requires a non-zero unsigned number, whereas the 2023 production uses unsigned_number.
The 2012 package and anonymous-program item alternatives lack interface_class_declaration and include overload_declaration among package declarations.
The 2017 package and anonymous-program item productions lack interface_class_declaration alternatives.
The 2012 parameter grammar has no forward_type option in a type-parameter declaration.
The 2017 type-parameter forms do not include the 2023 forward_type alternative.
The 2017 parameter-port grammar lacks the 2023 type_parameter_declaration form with optional forward_type.
The 2012 pattern production does not include the later parenthesized `( pattern )` alternative.
The 2017 pattern production lacks the parenthesized-pattern alternative added in 2023.
The 2012 primaries use empty_queue rather than empty unpacked-array concatenation and omit later select suffixes and constant-primary alternatives.
The 2017 constant_primary production does not include null, which is a constant-primary alternative in 2023.
The 2012 elaboration_system_task is the same accepted severity-task syntax under its earlier nonterminal name.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no final method or constraint specifier.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define the final_specifier construct.
The 2012 rule additionally permits the $ primary in open and coverage ranges, integer coverage expressions, and entire sequence or property actual arguments.
The 2012 Annex A struct-member rule does not impose the later guarantee restricting random qualifiers to unpacked structures.
The 2012 production and item nonterminal names differ, but the accepted randsequence forms are the same.
The 2012 source grammar lacks interface-class declarations and the later class final, implements, and default constructor-argument forms.
The 2017 source declaration grammar lacks interface-class declarations, class final specifiers, interface implementation lists, and default superclass-constructor arguments.
The 2017 path terminal identifier productions do not admit the interface_identifier.port_identifier forms added in 2023.
Increment/decrement is categorized directly as a statement item in 2012 rather than through blocking_assignment, without changing the accepted statement form.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no dynamic override specifier construct.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define dynamic override specifiers.
The 2012 grammar has only a basic quoted string production and no triple-quoted strings or bounded octal and hexadecimal escape productions.
The 2017 string literal grammar lacks triple-quoted strings and the bounded octal and hexadecimal escape productions added in 2023.
The 2012 system task/function call grammar lacks the later expression-list form with optional clocking event.
The 2012 task grammar has no dynamic override specifiers and does not permit static after ref in a task/function port direction.
The 2017 task declarations and prototypes do not admit the dynamic override specifiers defined by the 2023 grammar.
The 2012 rule states the restriction for implicit_class_handle, whose production includes this.
The 2012 event-control grammar separately admits hierarchical event identifiers and sequence identifiers rather than the later generalized clocking_event identifier forms.
The 2012 typedef grammar lacks incomplete class-scoped data types and uses interface_instance_identifier; its forward and nettype nonterminals also differ from the later forms.
The 2017 declaration grammar lacks incomplete class-scoped typedef types, interface-port typedefs, and the interface class forward-type form added in 2023.
The 2012 rule requires packed for a union with a packed dimension and has no soft-union alternative.
IEEE 1800-2017 requires packed for a union with a packed dimension and has no soft-union alternative; 2023 also permits soft.
The 2012 rule restricts the open range list to scalar or array variables, rather than the later singular-or-array wording.
The 2012 white_space production does not include formfeed.
